abstract: Long-read nanopore sequencing is a highly versatile technology that is currently constrained by high error-rates, which can impair accurate genotyping of complex DNA samples. Common mitigation strategies based on creating consensus sequences from tandem duplications synthesized by rolling-circle or multiple-displacement amplification are prone to create both chimeric DNA molecules and require an initial DNA-circularization. Here we present QuadSeq, a three-step DNA-synthesis technology that can convert linear DNA amplicons into duplicated DNA duplexes that encode two forward and two reverse strand copies of a sequence-of-interest. Intramolecular consensus sequences generated from QuadSeq duplicated DNA duplexes yielded a median single-amplicon accuracy of up to 0.9992 (Q31), without requiring a cumbersome DNA-circularization of the amplicon-of-interest. We can also show that the primary bottleneck for achieving accurate nanopore amplicon sequencing is not the mutation rate of the initial PCR-amplification, but the fidelity of the nanopore sequencing. QuadSeq consensus sequences generated from amplicons synthesized by a low-fidelity DNA polymerase (Taq) had a 6.6-fold lower median error-rate compared to amplicon simplex reads synthesized by a high-fidelity DNA polymerase (Phusion U). Going forward, we predict that the QuadSeq DNA-synthesis technology will enable the use of almost any low-fidelity DNA polymerase for high-fidelity nanopore amplicon sequencing.
